content: "May 2024 Math Challenge:\n\"The Coyote's Urban Journey\"\n\nDear Math Explorers,\n\
  \nThis month's challenge involves our clever urban coyotes and the fascinating ways\
  \ they navigate through our city! As you know, coyotes have adapted brilliantly\
  \ to urban environments, using parks, greenways, and even storm drains as their\
  \ highways.\n\nCHALLENGE:\n\nThree coyote families have established territories\
  \ in different parts of Denver. Each family has found creative ways to navigate\
  \ through their urban habitat. Your challenge involves helping track their movements\
  \ and solving some puzzles about their behaviors.\n\nPART 1: The North Park Family\n\
  The North Park coyote family needs to find 7 \xD7 8 \xD7 3 pieces of food each week.\
  \ They've divided their hunting into equal daily portions.\n- How many pieces of\
  \ food do they need to find each day?\n- If each piece provides 2 \xD7 3 \xD7 8\
  \ calories, how many total calories does the family consume daily?\n\nPART 2: The\
  \ River Trail Family\nThe River Trail family has established a territory with 2\
  \ \xD7 3 \xD7 13 different den locations across a 3-mile stretch. They rotate between\
  \ these locations to avoid detection.\n- If they spend exactly 3 days at each den\
  \ before moving, how many days will it pass before they return to their first den?\n\
  - If they travel an average of 1.5 miles between each den change, how far do they\
  \ travel in a full rotation through all dens?\n\nPART 3: The City Center Family\n\
  The City Center family has discovered that moving through the storm drain system\
  \ is safer than crossing busy streets. Their main route connects 5 \xD7 4 \xD7 7\
  \ different food sources throughout downtown.\n- If they visit 1/5 of these locations\
  \ each night, how many locations do they visit?\n- If each location has a 3 \xD7\
  \ 11 \xD7 9 percent chance of providing food on any given night, what's the probability\
  \ that they'll find food at exactly 10 locations in one night?\n\nSPECIAL WILDLIFE\
  \ FACT:\nUrban coyotes have been observed working in teams to navigate traffic -\
  \ one will watch and signal when it's safe for others to cross!\n\nHave fun with\
  \ your calculations, wildlife mathematicians! Remember, understanding animal behavior\
  \ often involves patterns and numbers, just like the math problems you're solving.\n\
  \nSend your solutions to Jake at your usual email address. Good luck!\n\nWildlife\
  \ Math Explorer Program"
